title: 14 vs 54 Vegan Lasagna: Budget-Friendly vs Luxe Plant-Based Lasagna
summary: In this Goodful video, Merle and Rachel stage a friendly, food-competition to contrast a vegan lasagna made on a tight budget with one made at a higher spend, aiming to show how flavor, texture, and yield can be balanced at different price points. They flip a coin to assign which cook handles the $14 versus the $54 version, and enlist Arya as a blind judge who doesn’t know who prepared which dish. The budget version builds a tofu-based ricotta and a mushroom-eggplant meat sauce, then bakes with simple sauce, noodles, and dried herbs. The upscale version uses cashews for a richer ricotta, a wine-enhanced meat sauce with San Marzano tomatoes, and a vegan cheese topping. After both are prepared and tasted, Arya weighs texture and flavor before the hosts reveal the costs and discuss which offers better value, even joking about combining elements from both recipes for a future “love child” version.

sections.title: Challenge setup and participants
sections.description: Merle and Rachel announce a friendly competition to make two vegan lasagnas at $14 and $54, plan to coin-toss budgets, and designate Arya as a blind judge who won't know who cooked which lasagna.

sections.title: Budget-friendly ricotta prep (tofu-based)
sections.description: For the $14 lasagna, the cook prepares a ricotta from extra-firm tofu with lemon juice, nutritional yeast, garlic, and dried basil, blending to a ricotta-like texture.

sections.title: Budget meat sauce (mushroom & eggplant)
sections.description: The budget version builds a meat sauce using olive oil, onion, garlic, cheaper mushrooms (white button) and eggplant for body, with a splash of soy sauce for umami and Italian seasoning, simmering with tomato sauce.

sections.title: Upscale ricotta prep (cashews)
sections.description: The $54 lasagna uses cashews blended with nutritional yeast, lemon juice, olive oil, basil, garlic, salt, pepper, and water to create a richer vegan ricotta.

sections.title: Upscale meat sauce (wine & San Marzano)
sections.description: The premium version adds wine and San Marzano tomatoes to the meat sauce, with tomato paste and Italian seasoning, and simmers for 25-30 minutes to deepen flavor.

sections.title: Lasagna assembly & baking (both versions)
sections.description: Both lasagnas are assembled with sauce on the bottom, layered with noodles, ricotta, meat mixture, and more sauce, then topped with vegan mozzarella and dried basil, covered and baked before finishing uncovered.

sections.title: Taste test and cost comparison
sections.description: Arya tastes both dishes, comments on texture and flavor, and the hosts compare total costs ($14 vs $54), discussing which version offers better value.

sections.title: Closing thoughts & viewer prompts
sections.description: The video wraps with reflections on budget-friendly cooking, the idea of combining elements from both versions, and a call for viewer suggestions on other 'rich vs broke' recipes.
